tasks.task: Size a market top-down and bottom-up

items.when: When a market needs sizing two ways with every number tagged given, sourced, derived or guessed
When you need published totals and want each one with a source link you can open
When you want a guided bottom-up estimate with a range and every number labelled
When you want a second estimate built another way to compare against the first
When the total looks huge, to test whether the market is drawn too wide
Before the estimate is shared, to give each input a dated source or mark it a guess

tasks.task: Compare 3 to 6 rivals on the same rows

items.when: When rivals must be compared on offer, price, buyer, proof, message and weak points
When you have rival links and need a first profile of each from their public pages
When you hold facts on one rival and need them set against the client's product
When the rivals are online stores and channels, prices and messages need a side-by-side
Before delivery, to check each rival price and claim has a dated public source

tasks.task: Rank the risks in an idea and pick one cheap test

items.when: Before recommending a product, reconcile contribution scenarios, thresholds and the final decision
When an idea must be tested for whether anyone will pay before money is spent building
Before choosing a test, to find the few guesses the idea stands on and rank them
When you want several cheap test types to compare, each with a pass mark
When the riskiest guess is known and you need the cheapest valid test and a fail line
When the test will run over weeks and someone must read the result and call it
When the idea has no clear edge and the founder says the market is everyone

tasks.task: Check demand from the evidence already in hand

items.when: When the client has sign-ups, quotes or pre-orders and asks if that is real demand
When you need the pains, objections and buying signals people post, with links
When you want a quick score for real problem, who needs it badly and the cheapest check
When the evidence is what people said, to weigh it against what they actually did
When demand looks real, to test market size and staying power and get a go or stop call

tasks.task: Map the gaps rivals leave open

items.when: When you know what buyers value and need a grid of where no rival is strong
When you want rivals plotted on two axes to find a corner the client can own
When the category is crowded, to look for gaps in price, reach, taste or buyer
When the gap may be in what rivals say, to compare messages from their public pages
When the gap report lists ten openings and the client needs the one idea to own

tasks.task: Design a short survey for one decision and analyse it

items.when: When one decision needs a neutral survey, a sample plan and a read of the answers
Before writing questions, to set the sample size for each segment you want to compare
When the draft exists, to get a bias review, a shorter list and a pretest plan
When answers are in and you need a checked findings table with honest caveats
Before a result is reported, to score how far each question's answers can be trusted

tasks.task: Map segments and pick the first one to win

items.when: When the product tries to please everyone and you need groups that buy differently
When you have reviews and survey answers, to group buyers by how they describe themselves
When you have customer data, to find natural groups by what people actually do
When each segment needs a profile card built from survey or customer data
When there are several possible first markets, to rank small ones and name one to own
When one starting segment must be chosen with a path from there to the mainstream

tasks.task: Write a short market snapshot for one idea

items.when: When the client needs a sourced report where sizing shows its assumptions
When the idea rides a trend and you must judge if it is real and at what stage
Before the snapshot recommends entry, to score size, trend risk and fit

tasks.task: Write a customer interview guide that gets the truth

items.when: Before talking to past or possible buyers, to ask what they did, not what they think
When draft questions exist, to fix the ones that pitch the idea or ask about the future
After each talk, to tell facts from praise and ideas and get the next question
When interviews run in rounds and the patterns should build from round to round

tasks.task: Compare rival prices and draw the takeaways

items.when: When rival prices, packs and terms must be laid on the same rows from public material
When the comparison must end in a recommended price from costs, rivals and value
When a price gap needs explaining by what each rival includes

tasks.task: Run a willingness-to-pay survey and read the price range

items.when: When the price questions need a sample, screening and consent wording around them
When you need the price questions to send this week and a way to read a best price
When price survey data is in and you need price points and good, better, best tiers
Before quoting a range, to check the sample and questions can carry it

tasks.task: Plan a price test for a site or sales calls

items.when: When you have costs and sales data and need a price to try with three outcome cases
When the test will run for weeks and needs reading and a next price set
When the test is a price rise, to score readiness from what buyers already say

tasks.task: Tear down one rival's funnel, ads and offer

items.when: When one rival needs a deep read of offer, proof, message and what customers say
When you can subscribe and buy, to note how the rival follows up and upsells
When their public ads and landing pages should be read, with proof kept apart from guesses

tasks.task: Run the monthly market and competitor watch

items.when: In the first week of each month, to log what changed and what it means
When you have this month's rival ads and pages and need changes since last month
Before the log is sent, to date and source each change it reports

tasks.task: Stress-test a business plan before money is committed

items.when: When a full plan exists and needs the strongest case against it and a pre-mortem
When you have the plan's key bets, to find which break first and what to test
When the plan has a budget, to run three bad-year tests and find its breaking point
When the plan looks fine on average and nobody has asked what could ruin it

tasks.task: Run a market entry research sprint to a decision

items.when: When money rides on a new product, segment, country, site or price change
When you must judge where profit comes from in the industry before entering
When you want forces, a counter-position and a first market in one guided run
When there are two ways in, to put both entry plans on a page with money and dates
When the sprint must end in a memo with the choice, risks and missing facts
When the entry case rests on a growing market and ignores who holds the power in it

tasks.task: Compare candidate locations with a weighted scorecard

items.when: When choosing a site between a few options and you want a fair comparison you can adjust
When the site is a second branch, to test whether the business runs without the owner
When the scores are close, to have a fresh reviewer pick one against the brief

tasks.task: Plan a service area or split sales territories

items.when: When areas or territories must be compared on customers, travel and size
Before the split, to turn messy sales rows into one report by territory and rep

tasks.task: Turn comparable sales into a pricing case for a seller

items.when: When an agent has sold data and needs a market analysis for a listing presentation
When the pricing case must become slides for the seller meeting
Before the meeting, to read the case as a seller who thinks the home is worth more

tasks.task: Choose the next export country

items.when: When there are three candidate countries and you want them compared on the same criteria
When you need a market pick, entry route, localisation list and rules to check
When the seller is an online store and shipping and tax costs drive the ranking
When the question is the order of markets, to rank them nearest first with a move sign
Before a country is picked, to check the margin after freight and duty
When the goods ship from the US, to see if a licence or exception applies

tasks.task: Write a distributor search brief and entry route options

items.when: When the country is picked and the brief must state why and on which criteria
When the choice is between a distributor, an agent and selling direct

tasks.task: Find and check sources for market facts

items.when: When a draft is written, to list every claim that needs a source and the kind to find
When figures came from the web, to check each against trusted sources with a confidence
When you hold many reports that disagree and need what is well backed and what is disputed

tasks.task: Check a research plan for ethics and privacy

items.when: Before fieldwork on any survey, interview round, competitor review or smoke test
When the study collects personal data, to see if it needs a fuller privacy review

always.when: Before any report leaves, to give each number a dated source or mark it as a guess
Before a report is shared, to catch typos and one segment or rival named two ways

helpers.when: When the answer needs a full interview round, focus group or review mining of customers
When research must become a price list, tiers and a rollout plan
When survey or sales data needs statistics, weighting or joining across files
When the gap report must become positioning, messaging and a launch plan
When the market case needs a financial model, payback and funding needs
When the findings need designed charts or a map, not tables

gaps: No library item compares candidate sites on catchment, footfall, rent and rivals nearby
No library item plans a service area, balances sales territories or writes a map brief for a cartographer
No library item builds a comparative market analysis from comparable home sales
No library item writes a monthly neighbourhood market update or an area comparison sheet for buyers
No library item writes a distributor search brief, distributor questions or an export readiness checklist
No library item analyses Van Westendorp or Gabor-Granger answers into an acceptable price range
No library item ranks features or packages by value with MaxDiff or a simple conjoint
No library item checks a research plan for consent, privacy and fair competitor research before fieldwork
No library item writes segment profile cards or a needs-by-segment matrix as its main job
No library item pulls official statistics such as census or trade data with source notes for sizing
No library item keeps a competitor change log that covers prices, hiring and reviews, not only ads and pages
